title: Defect-free EUV mask blanks and pellicles
bottleneck: EUV masks are reflective multilayer mirrors (40+ Mo/Si bilayers) where a single nanometer-scale defect can print on every die. Producing defect-free mask blanks at 2nm-class tolerances and protecting them with pellicles that transmit 13.5nm light without overheating remain unsolved manufacturing problems. High-NA's smaller depth of focus magnifies the impact of any mask imperfection.
why_it_blocks: Masks are the master template for the world's most expensive chips; uncorrectable mask defects become systematic yield loss across entire wafer lots. Without reliable blanks and pellicles, high-NA EUV cannot move from pilot lines to dependable high-volume production.
current_state: Pellicle materials with acceptable EUV transmission and thermal stability are emerging, and mask-shops have improved blank defect inspection. Still, defect-free blank supply is limited and expensive, and actinic inspection tools are scarce.
